articles.title: We Open Sourced Our Web Crawler. Here's How to Run a Node.
articles.excerpt: The crawler behind cl0q.com is now public. Anyone can read the code, run a node, and help index the open web. https://codeberg.org/cl0qsearch/crawler-node Search shouldn't be a black box. The big engi…
articles.body: The crawler behind cl0q.com is now public. Anyone can read the code, run a node, and help index the open web. https://codeberg.org/cl0qsearch/crawler-node Why open source it? Search shouldn't be a black box. The big engines don't tell you what they crawl, how they rank, or what they do with the data. We think that's wrong. cl0q is an independent search engine with its own crawler and index. We've mapped 38.5M domains so far, working toward 100M. Now the crawler itself is open for anyone to inspect, run, or improve. If you've ever wondered "what does a real web crawler look like under the hood," this is your answer. Every line is readable. No magic. What it does The node software discovers websites, fetches their homepages politely, and sends what it finds to cl0q's index. That's it.

articles.title: How to Write Your First Agent Skill
articles.excerpt: You have house rules for your coding agent: how commit messages should look, what a code review should check, how meeting notes should be structured. So you paste them into the chat at the start of ev…
articles.body: You have house rules for your coding agent: how commit messages should look, what a code review should check, how meeting notes should be structured. So you paste them into the chat at the start of every session — and by message ten the agent has drifted anyway. Next session, you paste again. The problem is not memory. The instructions live in your clipboard instead of in a file the agent loads every time. A skill is that file. What a skill is A skill is a folder containing one file: SKILL.md . It has two parts. The YAML frontmatter carries two fields — a name and a description . The description is the trigger: the agent scans the descriptions of its skills to decide which ones apply to your request.

articles.body: Don't hold your breath for a new Watch Dogs game anytime soon. As reported by Game File , Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot was asked by an investor about the future of the Watch Dogs franchise. The CEO noted that Ubisoft considers the IP "to be an important brand for the future" but neglected to explain how. Game File's Stephen Totilo stated that Guillemot suggested that there are no Watch Dogs games in active development at the moment, which suggests Ubisoft may still be figuring out where to take the series from here. There is a Watch Dogs movie on the horizon , but there's no word on when it will be released. The film wrapped production two years ago and had reshoots last year, but there hasn't been any sort of meaningful promotion for the film to date.
